threepl.nodes

Class BlockNode

  • java.lang.Object
    • threepl.nodes.Node
      • threepl.nodes.BlockNode
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    TDEConstants, Constant
    Direct Known Subclasses:
    ParBlockNode, SeqBlockNode, SyncBlockNode, WaitPriNode

    public class BlockNode
extends Node
implements Constant, TDEConstants
    This implements a code block. The statements within it are subnodes.

    Execution of statements within the block is carried out sequentially, however detailed execution control of break and continue statements is done here. Block execution is done through a call to method execute().

    If method execute() encounters a break, continue or return, the nodes for these (BreakNode, ContinNode and ReturnNode) return a status code which is detected. On getting a return status execute() itself returns immediately with that return status. The break and continue return status codes are eventually intercepted by an enclosing loop node (WhileNode, DoWhileNode or ForNode) which reacts accordingly. For a break the loop node will return (with a zero status code). For a continue the loop node will execute the next iteration. A return status code will cause execute methods to return with the same status code all the way back to a containing Module, Procedure or function.

      • execute

        public Constant.EXECR execute(TDEVar esig,
                              java.util.ArrayList<TDEVar> startl,
                              java.util.ArrayList<TDEVar> finishl,
                              QueueRefs queues,
                              boolean toplevel,
                              boolean availok,
                              QueueRefs checkedqueues,
                              TDEVar pri_in,
                              TDEVar pri_out)
        Execute a code block.
        Overrides:
        execute in class Node
        Parameters:
        esig - is an exception/restart signal, or null
        startl - is a list of start signals for target statements below this node
        finishl - is a list of finish signals for target statements below this node
        queues - returns all the queue availability signals accumulated from code below
        toplevel - is true if this is the top level in a module
        availok - is true if a previous sync makes a queue availability wait unnecessary
        checkedqueues - gives queue reads which have already been checked
        pri_in - is an optional input signal to a priority encoder
        pri_out - is an optional output signal from a priority encoder
        Returns:
        the EXECR.NONE, EXECR.break, EXECR.continue or EXECR.return status value
